_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 4 Computing unit lecture film, Lesson 7 Bitsy Loops. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow LESSON[lecture] in order (sensors; a sensor program; loops on the device; control systems; not a control system; the LED grid and the real board). Bitsy's board is a closure in the lesson kit and cannot be lifted, so the film DRAWS the board and borrows only the semantics: ART.device.inputs, ART.device.block, ART.device.plan and ART.kit.LED decide every block label and every LED pattern on every pass of the loop, so the film cannot disagree with the lesson about what a program does.
title: Bitsy Loops
subtitle: Grade 4 Computing
objectives: Know how to develop programs for a physical computing device to produce outputs from input devices.
Know how to develop programs for a physical computing device using count-controlled and indefinite (forever) loops.
Identify examples where a control system is used.

beats.say: Bitsy's button waits for a press. Its two sensors wait for nothing at all.
Add a loop, and Bitsy runs round and round all by itself.
Bitsy has five inputs. Button A, a shake sensor and a microphone.
Then two more: a temperature sensor and a light sensor.
A sensor is an input that senses by itself. Nobody presses a sensor.
The temperature sensor feels how warm it is. The light sensor sees how bright it is.
So a program starts with when the sensor senses something.

scenes.heading: When it gets hot, when it gets dark

beats.say: When it gets hot, turn the motor, show a smile.
That is a fan that starts itself. Nobody pressed anything.
When it gets dark, all lights on, beep. That is a night light.
The when block names the input. Press A, and this program does nothing.
A repeat block repeats the output after it, a counted number of times.
When A is pressed, repeat 3 times, beep. Count them: one, two, three.
Then it stops on its own. That is a count-controlled loop.
A forever block repeats everything after it. Lights on, wait, lights off, wait.
Round and round, a flashing light, until you press Stop.
A control system senses something, decides with a program, and acts.
A thermostat senses the cold and turns the heating on.
A street lamp senses the dark and lights up. Nobody flicks a switch.
A greenhouse senses the heat and opens its window.
Bitsy's night light does all three: sense, decide, act.
A candle, a pencil, a bicycle. Nothing senses and nothing decides.
A radio you switch on by hand is not one either.
A person decides every time. There is no program in the middle.
A control system decides by itself, from a sensor.
Look closely at Bitsy's screen. It is twenty-five little lights in a grid.
Count them: five across and five down.
Each little light is an LED. An LED uses very little power.
Show a heart switches some LEDs on and leaves the rest off.
A real board called the micro:bit has the same grid of LEDs.
You program it in MakeCode, and its blocks do what yours do.

at.blocks: its blocks do what yours do

beats.say: A sensor senses by itself. It never needs a press.
A repeat loop counts, then stops. A forever loop runs until Stop.
Bitsy's screen is twenty-five LEDs, switched on by your program.
Sense, decide, act. That is a control system, and it is all around you.
